en: The Compendium of the Womb.
Homage to the One of Great Compassion.
The waves of the oceans of suffering in the three worlds are stirred by karmic actions.
They have emerged from the tainted states, such as the wholesome and the unwholesome. ||1||
These [actions] arise from attachment, aversion, and so forth, which have the afflictions as their cause;
likewise, the cause for the emergence of those [afflictions] is the desirable, the undesirable, and so on. (2)
Arising from the grasping of duality, there occurs the grasping of objects and the grasper;
and [notions] such as permanence, omnipresence, and unity are the causes for the production of all [erroneous] things. (3)

Therefore, a fortunate man who desires liberation for both himself and the Supreme Self should dispel [this misconception] through the practice of sound reasonings, such as dependent origination. ||4||
First, one should grasp all phenomena, both internal and external;
then, one should regard them as equal to space, which is devoid of all defining characteristics. (5)
But having taken the entire world as his object, seeing it overwhelmed by the grasping at real entities, he was preceded by great compassion that dries up the ocean of suffering. (6)

One should cultivate the jewel of the awakening mind (bodhicitta), which brings about the welfare of oneself and others, as well as the great waves of the conduct of awakening, such as the six perfections and so forth. (7)
Through the practice of emerging from meditative absorption, one should proceed gradually by means of the five paths;
having severed the two kinds of obscurations and having fully perfected the two accumulations. (8)
The fruit to be attained is the three bodies (trikāya), and the characteristic of attaining the three bodies arises from the cloud of effortless compassion, which is emptiness like space. 9.
Constantly moistening the three realms day and night with streams of nectar from his two bodies, he ripens the harvest of merit from the excellent seeds at the seat of enlightenment. ||10||
This is the heart of all Buddhas, known as the "Collection of the Womb.
Due to the end of time, there will be short lifespans, many diseases, and meager enjoyments. (11)

Because of evil causes and many obstacles, and because one is unable to remain [in this world] for long, and since it is impossible to sever one's footprints [from past actions], one should indeed take refuge in a true friend. 12.
With a mind of supreme vigor, intensely mindful of the precipice, he quickly grasped the fetus in order to save both himself and the other. (13)
Through this merit created by this affection, may all unfortunate beings, becoming composed of the spirit of enlightenment (bodhicitta), swiftly enter the womb. 14.
The *Garbhasaṅgraha*, composed by the great master Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna, is completed.
